page: Microsoft Azure DC64ads_cc_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by the AMD EPYC 7763 processor, utilizing the x86_64 architecture. Operating under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this server provides 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 32 physical cores with 2 threads per core, running at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 256.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It features 2458 GB of local storage and is Premium Storage capable, though it does not include any GPU accelerators.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core and memory subsystem performance. The server achieves top-tier results in Passmark memory testing and strong performance in stress-ng multi-core CPU evaluations. Cryptographic and integer operations are supported by hardware-accelerated instructions like AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. Multi-threaded workloads, such as bzip3 decompression and software compilation with Clang, perform in the top 25% tier. However, memory bandwidth for uncached large blocks and single-threaded text processing remain in the average tier, and large-scale LLM inference is a notable bottleneck, scoring in the bottom 25% for 70B model text generation.

Given its balanced vCPU-to-RAM ratio and substantial local storage capacity, the DC64ads_cc_v5 offers high resource density for enterprise workloads. It is well-suited for database operations, as evidenced by strong Redis SET and Passmark database benchmark scores. The combination of dedicated AMD EPYC cores and high-capacity local storage makes it an efficient choice for multi-threaded application hosting, software build pipelines, and moderate data processing tasks, while avoiding the premium costs associated with specialized GPU or memory-heavy instances.
